newsitem.title: USA: Daschle sees danger of politicizing campaign probe.
newsitem.headline: Daschle sees danger of politicizing campaign probe.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Monday a planned probe of party fund-raising was close to becoming politicized and called for a cut-off date.

The Republican chairman of the Senate investigating committee, Fred Thompson, has asked for $6.5 million to investigate reports of illegal foreign donations, special White House favours to donors and other activities.
"I think we're close to politicizing this matter and I don't want to do that," Daschle told reporters.

He said he was not accusing the Tennessee senator of seeking to politicize the investigation but he charged that Thompson and others had apparently assumed that fund-raising irregularities by the Democratic National Committee were on the same scale as the Watergate scandal.
Thompson, a lawyer, was Republican counsel on the Senate Watergate Committee that investigated the scandal that eventually drove President Richard Nixon from office.
"My concern is that this not go on for years and years," Daschle said. "These investigations tend to take on a life of their own."

He called for a date to be set for completing the investigation and an evaluation of the allegations before setting a budget. He said the $6.5 million request was three times the amount the Senate spent on its Whitewater investigation involving the Clintons.
Last week Thompson appealed to the Senate Rules Committee to allocate the funds but faced strong opposition from Democrats. The committee took no action and has not set a new meeting on the issue.

Any funding must be approved by the full Senate, where it could face a Democratic filibuster. Daschle said Democrats were not coordinating with the White House in seeking to set limits on the investigation.
